product: Certificate Assistant is a hackathon decision-support tool for Chhattisgarh caste and domicile certificates: it links an applicant to relatives' archived certificates and drafts orders, with the officer deciding.
architecture: There is no LLM in this repo. An applicant record is normalised, blocked against a synthetic certificate archive and scored by a Splink-trained Fellegi-Sunter model exported to JSON. Rules produce flags and a checklist; bilingual Jinja2 templates draft orders and messages, and an entity checker verifies them against the source record. The browser runs OCR and QR decoding locally and sends only a perceptual hash. Officers confirm or dismiss each match, and those acts feed a ridge-regularised recalibration. Evaluation is on held-out synthetic families. The 'AI' chapters map to classical retrieval, evals, guardrails and product UX only.

evidence.concept: Blocking indexes as an inverted index over name keys
evidence.what: Candidate generation looks up three precomputed dict indexes (district+surname skeleton, village, given+surname skeleton) and unions the hits, so only a few certificates are scored instead of the whole archive.
evidence.lesson: Same idea as an inverted index: cheap recall-oriented candidate generation first, expensive scoring second.

evidence.concept: Analyzer for Indian names (transliterate, fold, skeleton)
evidence.snippet:
Pipeline for one name string:
  1. strip honorifics / relation markers (Shri, Smt, श्री, S/O, पिता ...)
  2. Devanagari -> Latin with indic_transliteration (ITRANS) + Hindi schwa deletion
  3. lowercase, phonetic folding (aa->a, ee->i, w->v, sh->s, ksh->x ...),
     collapse doubled letters ("Markaam" -> "markam")
  4. tokens; surname = last token; given = the rest joined WITHOUT spaces
     ("Ram Lal" == "Ramlal")
  5. consonant skeleton = folded string with vowels removed
"""
evidence.what: One normalisation pipeline (strip honorifics, Devanagari to Latin, phonetic folding, consonant skeleton) is shared by training and runtime so both sides tokenise names identically.
evidence.lesson: Index-time and query-time analyzers must be the same code; here the same module serves Splink training and the live scorer.

evidence.concept: Graded fuzzy comparison levels for a name field
evidence.what: A name pair is bucketed into null, exact, skeleton, Jaro-Winkler >=0.92, >=0.80 or else. Each bucket later gets a learned weight, so fuzziness is graded rather than a single threshold.

evidence.concept: Score fusion by summing learned log-odds weights
evidence.snippet:
def log2_odds(self, levels: dict[str, str]) -> float:
        return self.model.prior + sum(self.model.weight(k, lv) for k, lv in levels.items())
evidence.what: The final score is the model prior plus the weight of each field's comparison level (naive-Bayes style Fellegi-Sunter), then converted to a probability. This is the classical-ML analogue of fusing several retrieval signals.
evidence.lesson: RRF fuses ranks; this fuses calibrated evidence. The weights come from EM, not hand tuning.

evidence.concept: Relevance expressed as a calibrated match probability
evidence.what: Two tiers decide what the officer sees: >=0.95 'exact' and >=0.60 'possible'; below 0.60 nothing is shown. The probability is the relevance judgment.

evidence.concept: Metadata filter: like-for-like certificate kind and LGD place levels
evidence.what: Candidates are filtered by certificate kind (caste vs domicile) before scoring, and place comparison uses Local Government Directory codes, i.e. structured metadata rather than free text.
evidence.lesson: Evidence of the wrong kind is excluded up front rather than down-weighted.

evidence.concept: Precision/recall/F1 and recall that counts blocking misses
evidence.what: Every true link the blocking never surfaced is added as a score-0 positive, so end-to-end recall is not flattered by a candidate generator that dropped relatives.
evidence.lesson: Recall must be measured over the whole corpus, not only over the candidates the retriever returned.

evidence.concept: Slice metrics: precision/recall per cohort
evidence.snippet:
slice_defs = [

        ("plains", {"en": "Plains divisions (Raipur, Durg, Bilaspur)", "hi": "मैदानी संभाग (रायपुर, दुर्ग, बिलासपुर)"}),
        ("women", {"en": "Women applicants", "hi": "महिला आवेदक"}),

    ]
evidence.what: Metrics are reported separately for hard same-village cases, tribal divisions, plains, women and cross-script pairs rather than one global number.
evidence.lesson: Slices expose where a system fails for specific groups; matches the chapter on failure taxonomies.

evidence.concept: Held-out eval set built from generator ground truth
evidence.snippet:
"""Evaluate the lineage matcher on HELD-OUT synthetic families (30% of lineages, never used
for training) against the generator's ground truth. Writes model/eval.json in the
/api/eval shape.

A candidate pair is (applicant, archived certificate). It is a TRUE link when the
certificate holder is the applicant's father or a sibling (ground truth from
population.csv). Recall counts every true link in the archive, including those the
blocking never surfaced (so blocking misses are counted as misses).
evidence.what: Evaluation uses 30% of synthetic lineages never used for training, scored against the generator's known father/sibling truth.
evidence.lesson: Honest about being synthetic; real-archive accuracy is explicitly deferred.

evidence.concept: Failure slices as a taxonomy of hard cases
evidence.what: Each scored pair is tagged with slice labels (tribal division, plains, women) so errors can be grouped; hard and cross-script tags are added below.

evidence.concept: Synthetic officer labels with injected error rate
evidence.snippet:
def simulated_labels() -> list[dict]:
    u = universe()
    shown = [p for p in u["pairs"] if p["part"] == "pool" and _p(p["s"]) >= POSSIBLE]
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    out = []
    for p in rng.sample(shown, min(N_SIMULATED, len(shown))):
        y = p["y"]
        if rng.random() < OFFICER_ERROR:
            y = 1 - y
        out.append({"pair_id": p["id"], "y": y, "source": "simulated", "officer_error": y != p["y"]})
    return out
evidence.what: 300 simulated officer confirmations are drawn from ground truth with a 3% flipped-label rate, labelled 'simulated' everywhere, to exercise the learning loop when few real labels exist.
evidence.lesson: Injecting annotator noise is a good habit; the label is tagged so it is never mistaken for a real one.

evidence.concept: Honesty note on every eval result
evidence.what: The eval output carries a bilingual note saying the numbers are measured on synthetic data and must be re-measured on a labelled real sample before any pilot.
evidence.lesson: Expectation setting shipped in the data, not just in a slide.

evidence.concept: Calibrating the scorer against human (officer) labels with ridge shrinkage
evidence.what: Officer 'same family' / 'not this family' labels fit a ridge-regularised logistic recalibration shrunk toward the EM weights, so a few hundred labels cannot swing the model.
evidence.lesson: Validate an automated judge against human labels; here the human labels also tune it.

evidence.concept: Implicit feedback: officer dispositions become training labels
evidence.what: Each officer confirmation or dismissal on a live file is converted to a labelled pair with its model features; approve/reject decisions are deliberately not used as labels.
evidence.lesson: Choosing which user acts count as labels is the key design decision.

evidence.concept: In-browser OCR worker served from own origin
evidence.what: tesseract.js is loaded lazily as a single shared worker with local wasm and language data (English first, then Hindi), with a progress listener for the UI.
evidence.lesson: English-first language order is an empirical fix: Hindi-first garbled digits in certificate numbers.

evidence.concept: OCR confidence per field, low confidence shown as 'unclear' not 'mismatch'
evidence.what: A text mismatch is downgraded to 'unclear' when the field's OCR confidence is under 60, so a shaky read never reads as a finding against the applicant.

evidence.concept: Rule-based field extraction from OCR text
evidence.what: Regexes pull name and father from affidavit and certificate prose. Deterministic and offline, but brittle to any wording change; no model or schema-constrained extraction.
evidence.lesson: An LLM or layout model with a typed schema would handle wording drift; the regexes are fine for three known paper types.

evidence.concept: Typed request schema validates the fingerprint input
evidence.snippet:
class Fingerprint(BaseModel):
    app_id: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=40)
    phash: str = Field(pattern=r"^[0-9a-f]{16}$")
    kind: str = Field(default="unknown", max_length=20)
    label: str = Field(default="", max_length=80)
evidence.what: A Pydantic model constrains the perceptual hash to 16 hex digits and bounds the string lengths before any logic runs.
evidence.lesson: Not LLM output, but the same validate-at-the-boundary habit.

evidence.concept: Data minimisation: only a perceptual hash leaves the browser
evidence.snippet:
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ duplicate-paper check (perceptual hash)
# The browser sends only a 64-bit perceptual hash (pHash, DCT-based, as in Python's imagehash) of the page image —
# never the image. A rescan or a tilted phone photo of the same paper lands within a few bits (synthetic aff.png vs
# aff_noisy.jpg: 4 bits; different papers: >= 18). Held in memory, cleared by a demo reset.
evidence.what: The page image is never uploaded; the browser sends a 64-bit DCT perceptual hash, and the server compares hash distances to flag the same paper on another file.

evidence.concept: Reviewed Jinja2 templates with StrictUndefined as versioned 'prompts'
evidence.what: All citizen-message wording lives in reviewed .j2 files; StrictUndefined makes a missing variable a hard error. This is the template-bound alternative to generating text with a model.
evidence.lesson: If an LLM were added, it would sit behind the entity checker below.

evidence.concept: Entity checker validates finished output against the source record
evidence.what: Every number, certificate id and name-like word in the message must appear in the template's fixed wording or the source record; anything else is returned as an unsupported entity.
evidence.lesson: Docstring says it is the same guard an LLM rewrite would have to pass.

evidence.concept: Grounding: message checked against only the records used
evidence.what: The message is rendered from the case data, then checked with the application, office, service and deficiencies as the allowed source set.

evidence.concept: Unit test proves the guard catches invented entities
evidence.snippet:
def test_entity_checker_catches_invented_entities():
    from messages import check_entities
    app = client.get(f"/api/applications/{enc(HERO)}").json()["application"]
    ok = check_entities({"en": f"Namaste Sunita Markam. Your application {HERO} is APPROVED.", "hi": ""}, [app])
    assert ok["passed"]
    bad = check_entities({"en": f"Namaste Sunita Markam. Certificate CG/KDG/SDO/2011/999999 for Rahul, fee 500.", "hi": ""}, [app])
    assert not bad["passed"] and "CG/KDG/SDO/2011/999999" in bad["unsupported_entities"] and "500" in bad["unsupported_entities"]
evidence.what: A positive case passes and a message with an invented certificate number and fee '500' fails with both listed as unsupported entities.
evidence.lesson: Guardrails need their own positive and adversarial tests.

evidence.concept: Workflow, not an agent: the 'Certificate Assistant agent' never decides
evidence.snippet:
"""Round 8b: the visible "प्रमाण एजेंट" trace — what the system did for one file, step by step.

Built only from the real analysis and the timing marks engine.analyse() records while it runs (additive; the
analysis itself is unchanged). Honest labels: the agent reads, searches, scores, checks and drafts. It never decides.
The last step is always "waiting for the officer"; the frontend shows it as done once the file is decided.
"""
evidence.what: The module documents that the 'agent' only reads, searches, scores, checks and drafts, and that the last step is always the officer. It is a fixed pipeline of rules and one ML scorer.
evidence.lesson: Honest labelling: a deterministic workflow with a human final step.

evidence.concept: Step-by-step trace of one file's analysis
evidence.what: The trace ends with a mandatory 'waiting for the officer' step and numbers the steps; earlier steps carry timings and a status of ok, attention or waiting.

evidence.concept: Per-stage latency and count metrics
evidence.snippet:
if stats is not None:
            stats.update({"archive_certs": len(self.archive.certs), "blocked_views": len(set(cand)),
                          "candidates": len(best), "above_threshold": len(out),

evidence.concept: Collapsible trace with step icons and timings
evidence.what: A one-line summary (steps, total ms, items to check) opens into the full list; the officer step flips to 'Decided by the officer' only once decided.

evidence.concept: Approval gate: reject needs show-cause, approve needs every possible match disposed
evidence.what: The server returns 422 unless a show-cause reply is recorded before rejection, and unless every possible family record has been marked 'same' or 'not' before approval.
evidence.lesson: Human approval enforced in the API, not just the UI.

evidence.concept: Reversibility: undo a confirmation until the decision is signed
evidence.snippet:
@app.post("/api/applications/{app_id:path}/clear-match")
def clear_match(app_id: str, body: ClearMatchBody):
    """Undo a 'same family' / 'not this family' act — allowed until the decision is signed."""
    e = STATE.entry(app_id)
    _pending_or_409(e["application"])
    an = STATE.analysis(app_id)
    _match_or_400(an, body.cert_no)
    with STATE.lock:
        prev = STATE.dispositions.get(app_id, {}).pop(body.cert_no, None)
        STATE.invalidate(app_id)
    if prev is None:
        raise HTTPException(400, f"no confirmation or dismissal recorded for {body.cert_no}")
    an = STATE.analysis(app_id)
evidence.what: clear-match removes a 'same family' or 'not this family' act while the file is still pending, and the audit trail records the withdrawal.

evidence.concept: Audit log of every record access and decision
evidence.what: Each action is appended with timestamp, role, actor, action and the records accessed, then persisted.
evidence.lesson: Logs records touched; no prompts exist here, but the pattern carries over.

evidence.concept: UX that states facts and never pre-selects an outcome
evidence.snippet:
/**
 * Round 3: ONE evidence verdict at the top of the case view. It answers, in fixed rows and fixed icons,
 * what the evidence is, what the officer must decide, what needs attention, what the file relies on and
 * what is missing. Every other restatement of the same facts was removed from the page.
 * It states facts and the officer's task; it never pre-selects an outcome (round-2 anti-anchoring).
 */
evidence.what: One fixed-row evidence verdict tells the officer what is known and what they must decide; it avoids anchoring the decision on the machine's guess.

evidence.what: Five verdict states (match, spelling variant, differs - check original, unclear read, n/a) express certainty and avoid a binary fake/genuine label.

evidence.snippet:
if not c:
        # returned (not raised): the app-wide handler flattens HTTPException details to a string
        return JSONResponse(status_code=404, content={"found": False, "cert_no": no, "detail": {"en": f"No record {no} in the archive. This is not a ground for rejection; "

                                  "hi": f"अभिलेखागार में {no} का अभिलेख नहीं मिला। यह अस्वीकृति का आधार नहीं है; "

evidence.what: When the archive has no matching record, the API returns a 404 payload telling the officer this is not grounds for rejection and to check the original paper.

evidence.concept: One-tap explicit feedback schema
evidence.what: The officer rates the check with yes, no or wrong_family and an optional note, after the decision is made.

evidence.concept: Feedback pitfalls: one tap per decision and never an officer metric
evidence.snippet:
if d.get("tool_feedback"):  # one tap per decision; a repeat would silently flip the Collector's feedback tile
        raise HTTPException(409, "tool feedback is already recorded for this decision")
    with STATE.lock:
        d["tool_feedback"] = {"useful": body.useful, "note": (body.note or "").strip() or None,
                              "ts": datetime.now(IST).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
        d["snapshot"]["tool_feedback"] = d["tool_feedback"]
    STATE.add_audit(STATE.entries[app_id]["application"]["routed_to"], "tool_feedback", app_id, [],
                    note=f"Tool feedback (for improving the tool, not an officer metric): {body.useful}"
                         + (f" — {body.note.strip()}" if (body.note or "").strip() else ""))
evidence.what: A repeat submission returns 409 so it cannot flip the dashboard tile, and the audit note says the feedback is for the tool, not for judging the officer.
